examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For a piecewise function at a join, first match one-sided values to the function value, then match one-sided derivatives. Differentiability implies continuity; continuity alone does not imply differentiability. For max/min or absolute-value functions, locate branch crossings and compare actual active branches on both sides rather than differentiating one formula globally.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
f(x)=ax+b for x<2 and x² for x≥2. If f is differentiable at 2, find a+b.

**Answer: 0.** The right derivative at 2 is 4, so a=4. Continuity requires 2a+b=4, giving b=−4. Therefore a+b=0. Both conditions are necessary.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A derivative may exist where the second derivative does not. Keep claims about f, f′ and f″ separate when testing smoothness.

Continuity does not imply differentiability.
